fields.before: In nearly 300 patients, how loud the tinnitus measured in the clinic was had little relation to how much it bothered people; distress tracked better with depression, sound intolerance and how the sound was perceived. That supports the widespread clinical experience that reducing distress, not just the volume of the sound, is what matters for quality of life.
fields.after: In nearly 300 patients, how loud the tinnitus measured in the clinic was had little relation to how much it bothered people; distress tracked better with depression, sound intolerance and how the sound was perceived.

fields.before: A cross-sectional correlational study (N=293) in a single clinical setting reporting that tinnitus handicap (THI) is independently associated with subjective pitch, sound intolerance and depressive symptoms, while psychoacoustically matched tinnitus intensity was NOT associated with THI (and its correlation with subjective loudness did not survive Bonferroni correction). It adds another dataset reinforcing the known dissociation between measured loudness and distress. No effect sizes, correlation coefficients or p-values are given in the available abstract. Reported directionally: THI correlated positively with subjective loudness, pitch, complexity, sound intolerance, BDI and GAD-7; no significant association between THI and psychoacoustic tinnitus intensity; after Bonferroni correction, psychoacoustic intensity vs subjective loudness, psychoacoustic intensity vs THI-Functional, duration vs subjective loudness, subjective loudness vs BDI/GAD-7, and age vs subjective loudness/pitch were no longer significant.
fields.after: A cross-sectional correlational study (N=293) in a single clinical setting reporting that tinnitus handicap (THI) is independently associated with subjective pitch, sound intolerance and depressive symptoms, while psychoacoustically matched tinnitus intensity was NOT associated with THI (and its correlation with subjective loudness did not survive Bonferroni correction). No effect sizes, correlation coefficients or p-values are given in the available abstract. Reported directionally: THI correlated positively with subjective loudness, pitch, complexity, sound intolerance, BDI and GAD-7; no significant association between THI and psychoacoustic tinnitus intensity; after Bonferroni correction, psychoacoustic intensity vs subjective loudness, psychoacoustic intensity vs THI-Functional, duration vs subjective loudness, subjective loudness vs BDI/GAD-7, and age vs subjective loudness/pitch were no longer significant.

It adds no new patient data and no pooled effect estimates. 4974 records identified, 2690 unique records screened, 20 studies included; indication categories: tinnitus n=8, dysphagia n=3, vestibular disorders/rehabilitation n=3, Menière's disease n=2, olfactory dysfunction n=2, pharyngeal dysesthesia n=1, LPR-related disorders n=1. No pooled effect sizes reported.

fields.before: First reasonably sized evaluation of ambient pressure tympanometry (APT) as a bedside screening test for finding a radiologic cause of subjective pulsatile tinnitus — and it performs poorly (sensitivity ~43–57%, specificity ~54–57%), essentially no better than chance. This is diagnostic-workup evidence, not treatment evidence. 63/137 ears (46%) had a pulse-synchronous APT pattern; 51 (37.2%) had a radiologic correlate; 65 (44.2%) received a surgeon diagnosis. For a radiologic correlate: sensitivity 51%, specificity 57%, PPV 41.3%, NPV 66.2%. For a surgeon diagnosis: sensitivity 43.1%, specificity 54.9%, PPV 43.1%, NPV 54.9%. Chief-complaint subgroup (116 ears): radiologic correlate 56.9%/54.2%/46%/55.2%; surgeon diagnosis 43.6%/54.1%/46.2%/51.6%.
fields.after: An evaluation of ambient pressure tympanometry (APT) as a bedside screening test for finding a radiologic cause of subjective pulsatile tinnitus — and its sensitivity and specificity were low (sensitivity ~43–57%, specificity ~54–57%). This is diagnostic-workup evidence, not treatment evidence. 63/137 ears (46%) had a pulse-synchronous APT pattern; 51 (37.2%) had a radiologic correlate; 65 (44.2%) received a surgeon diagnosis. For a radiologic correlate: sensitivity 51%, specificity 57%, PPV 41.3%, NPV 66.2%. For a surgeon diagnosis: sensitivity 43.1%, specificity 54.9%, PPV 43.1%, NPV 54.9%. Chief-complaint subgroup (116 ears): radiologic correlate 56.9%/54.2%/46%/55.2%; surgeon diagnosis 43.6%/54.1%/46.2%/51.6%.

fields.before: A cross-sectional case-control ABR study reporting that middle-aged adults with tinnitus and normal audiograms/DPOAEs show selective wave I abnormalities (reduced amplitude at low intensity; prolonged latency in chronic tinnitus) plus suprathreshold changes (steeper wave V latency-intensity slope, higher V/I ratio) that differ by tinnitus duration. The chronicity-dependent stratification (acute <6 months vs chronic ≥6 months) is the main novel element; cochlear-synaptopathy-style ABR findings in tinnitus with normal hearing are themselves a long-contested literature. Pure-tone thresholds, wave V thresholds and DPOAEs did not differ across groups. Chronic tinnitus: prolonged wave I latency at 55, 75 and 80 dB nHL; steeper wave V latency-intensity slope; higher V/I ratio at 80 dB nHL. Both acute and chronic tinnitus: reduced wave I amplitude at 45 dB nHL. Interpeak latencies and wave V ABR growth ratio showed no robust group differences. No effect sizes, confidence intervals or exact p-values are given in the abstract.
fields.after: A cross-sectional case-control ABR study reporting that middle-aged adults with tinnitus and normal audiograms/DPOAEs show selective wave I abnormalities (reduced amplitude at low intensity; prolonged latency in chronic tinnitus) plus suprathreshold changes (steeper wave V latency-intensity slope, higher V/I ratio) that differ by tinnitus duration. The study stratifies the findings by tinnitus duration (acute <6 months vs chronic ≥6 months). Pure-tone thresholds, wave V thresholds and DPOAEs did not differ across groups. Chronic tinnitus: prolonged wave I latency at 55, 75 and 80 dB nHL; steeper wave V latency-intensity slope; higher V/I ratio at 80 dB nHL. Both acute and chronic tinnitus: reduced wave I amplitude at 45 dB nHL. Interpeak latencies and wave V ABR growth ratio showed no robust group differences. No effect sizes, confidence intervals or exact p-values are given in the abstract.

fields.before: A Norwegian naturalistic (uncontrolled, single-arm) service-evaluation of an internet-delivered program combining tinnitus retraining therapy and CBT in 144 patients, reporting THI change to 180 days with effect sizes stratified by baseline severity (largest change in the severe+ group). The severity-stratified reporting is the main novel element; the overall finding that guided digital CBT-type programs reduce tinnitus distress is already well established by controlled trials. THI pre-treatment to 180 days: d = 0.41 for the total sample; d = 0.95 for severe+ tinnitus; d = 0.22 for mild tinnitus. Small improvements in anxiety, depression and hyperacusis; no change in misophonia. Absolute THI point changes, confidence intervals, and attrition not given in the abstract.

fields.before: A large population-based cross-sectional analysis (Hoveyzeh Cohort, n=10,009) in southwestern Iran reporting a 10.5% self-reported tinnitus prevalence and an independent association between ICHD-3-defined chronic headache and tinnitus (adjusted OR 1.81). fields.before: First systematic ICF-based content analysis quantifying how much the items of six standard tinnitus distress questionnaires (THI, TQ, mTQ, THQ, TRQ, TFI) overlap in content with seven depression questionnaires, showing overlap ranges from ~12% (TQ) to ~73% (TRQ). It is a measurement/construct-validity paper, not treatment evidence. Depression questionnaires covered 14 second-level ICF categories vs 23 for tinnitus distress questionnaires. Seven categories were shared: energy and drive, sleep, attention, emotional, thought functions, interpersonal interactions and relationships, recreation and leisure. Overlap with depression instruments: TQ lowest at 11.54–26.92%, TRQ highest at 61.54–73.08%. Among depression scales: SDS least overlap with tinnitus scales (40–60%), DASS-42 depression subscale most (85.71–100%).

fields.before: Donepezil, a drug used in dementia, was tested for tinnitus for the first time in a placebo-controlled trial and did not work better than placebo on tinnitus severity or on measurements of the sound itself. Negative results like this are useful because they help rule out repurposed drugs and discourage off-label prescribing based on theory alone.

42710361.justification: The flag was raised because the item says this is the first randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of donepezil in chronic tinnitus. The paper's abstract and full text both say donepezil "has not yet been evaluated in individuals with tinnitus" (Clinics, 2026; PMC13573712), so the claim is supported by the authors' own statement and no correction is needed for it. The item has a separate correction (N4) for a different sentence.
